question: Why does neural collapse arise when classification networks are trained with mean squared error, and can exact dynamics be derived after the classifier approaches its feature-conditional least-squares optimum?

key_findings.claim: Neural collapse is empirically visible under vanilla MSE on the paper's selected ten-class image tasks.
key_findings.evidence: Across VGG, ResNet, and DenseNet trained on MNIST, FashionMNIST, SVHN, CIFAR-10, and STL-10, the appendix plots decreasing within-class variability, increasingly equiangular/equinorm class means and classifiers, self-duality, and convergence toward nearest-class-center decisions.

key_findings.claim: The MSE objective admits an exact least-squares-plus-deviation decomposition.
key_findings.evidence: For fixed extended features, Proposition 1 gives the ridge least-squares classifier. Theorem 1 writes total loss as an optimal-classifier term depending only on features plus a nonnegative quadratic term that is zero exactly when the learned classifier equals that optimum.

key_findings.claim: The least-squares component separates a within-class-collapse term from a class-mean/classifier geometry term.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 2 decomposes the least-squares loss into L_NC1, involving within-class covariance and the least-squares classifier, and L_NC2/3, measuring failure of class means and least-squares classifiers to form the target identity/ETF geometry.

key_findings.claim: Measured training trajectories motivate, but do not prove, that real networks remain on the proposed central path.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 2 shows the classifier-deviation term becoming small relative to the least-squares component early in the reported runs. The theory then replaces approximate proximity with the exact constraint W=W_LS(H), so the theoretical trajectory is not the original network training trajectory.

key_findings.claim: Under continually renormalized gradient flow on the central path, the signal-to-noise singular values grow and equalize with explicit asymptotics.
key_findings.evidence: With zero global mean, full-rank within-class covariance, no weight decay, unconstrained features, and projection onto identity within-class covariance, Proposition 2 gives an implicit closed form c1 log omega_j+c2 omega_j^2+c3 omega_j^4=a_j+t; Corollary 1 yields omega_j asymptotic to the fourth root of t/c3 and max/min ratio tending to one.

key_findings.claim: The exact flow implies all four neural-collapse properties for renormalized features, not an unconditional theorem about practical deep networks.
key_findings.evidence: Corollary 2 derives the limiting simplex-ETF orientation from the initial SNR singular vectors and invokes prior implications from NC1--NC2 to NC3--NC4. Its objects are the continually whitened, layer-peeled features under the exact central-path assumptions.

key_findings.claim: Terminal training improves reported test accuracy and robustness on average, but exceptions and test-set collapse complicate a generalization interpretation.
key_findings.evidence: Table 1 reports median and mean test-accuracy gains of 0.962 and 1.833 percentage points after zero training error, and Figure 9 reports robustness improvement. DenseNet-SVHN slightly loses accuracy, STL10-ResNet/DenseNet behave anomalously, and test-feature collapse is much slower and weaker than training-feature collapse.

method.core_idea: Exploit the algebraic tractability of MSE by eliminating the last-layer classifier through least squares, identify a feature-only central path, whiten within-class covariance, and solve the resulting gradient-flow dynamics through the singular values of a class-mean signal-to-noise matrix.
method.mechanism: Augment features to absorb bias; decompose ridge MSE into the loss of W_LS(H) and a positive classifier-deviation quadratic; decompose the feature-only loss into NC1 and NC2/3 terms; restrict to W=W_LS(H), lambda=0, zero-centered unconstrained features; continually map features to identity within-class covariance; project gradients onto that manifold; derive and integrate the decoupled SNR singular-value ODEs.
assumptions: Balanced classes with C classes and N examples per class
The learned last-layer classifier is exactly on the feature-conditional least-squares central path
Last-layer features may be optimized as unconstrained variables rather than outputs of earlier network layers
Weight decay is set to zero in the exact dynamics
The feature global mean is zero
Within-class covariance stays full rank so inverse-square-root whitening exists
Training follows continuous projected gradient flow with continual covariance renormalization
The selected MSE datasets do not require the scaling heuristic needed for larger class counts

techniques.role: Separates feature geometry from last-layer classifier suboptimality exactly.
Eliminates the classifier by constraining it to its conditional MSE optimum.
Assigns feature-only MSE terms to within-class collapse and ETF/self-dual geometry.
Chooses a representative coordinate system invariant under least-squares predictions.
Keeps renormalized features at identity within-class covariance.
Reduces collapse to growth and equalization of class-separation singular values.

evaluations.setting: 15 MSE-trained dataset-architecture combinations from five ten-class image datasets and VGG/ResNet/DenseNet
evaluations.metric: NC1--NC4 diagnostics and the three MSE decomposition terms over epochs
evaluations.result: most curves approach neural-collapse geometry and the classifier-deviation term becomes comparatively negligible early
evaluations.baseline: corresponding CE neural-collapse measurements and exact least-squares classifier behavior

evaluations.setting: test accuracy from the first zero-training-error epoch through the final epoch
evaluations.result: median improvement 0.962 and mean improvement 1.833, with individual exceptions
evaluations.baseline: accuracy at first zero training error

evaluations.result: MSE curves generally collapse faster and report greater robustness in the plotted comparisons
evaluations.baseline: measurements released with the foundational CE neural-collapse study

evaluations.result: collapse remains visible for several combinations but is slower and ends substantially above training-data collapse
evaluations.baseline: the same statistic on training features

evaluations.result: all nonzero singular values diverge at fourth-root rate and equalize, implying NC1--NC4 in the model
evaluations.baseline: unconstrained-feature neural-collapse analyses without these exact renormalized dynamics

limitations: The exact theorem concerns a continually whitened unconstrained-feature flow, not the parameter dynamics of VGG, ResNet, or DenseNet.
Central-path proximity is measured empirically; exact restriction discards classifier-feature lag and coupling.
The theoretical analysis removes weight decay despite using weight decay in the empirical training setting.
Zero global mean, balanced classes, and full-rank within-class covariance exclude common imbalanced or degenerate cases.
CIFAR-100 and ImageNet are omitted because vanilla MSE needs an additional scaling heuristic there.
The experimental grid appears to use one selected run per dataset-architecture combination rather than uncertainty across seeds.
STL-10 combinations show slow or inconsistent collapse, and the authors offer hypotheses rather than tests.
Training-set neural collapse is much stronger than test-set collapse, so its relation to generalization remains unresolved.
Batch normalization, SGD noise, weight decay, and architecture are not ablated independently.
failure_modes: A practical trajectory can depart from the central path even when the deviation term is small relative to a dominant loss component.
Whitening becomes ill-conditioned as within-class covariance approaches rank deficiency.
Continuous renormalization can create dynamics that no realizable network parameterization follows.
Class imbalance changes the centered target geometry away from the balanced simplex ETF.
MSE logit scaling for many classes can prevent the empirical phenomenon without additional tuning.
Near-perfect train collapse can coexist with weaker or absent collapse on test data.
A dataset-architecture pair can converge too slowly for terminal behavior to appear within the compute budget.
Terminal accuracy or robustness changes can be attributed to continued training rather than collapse itself.
reusable_insights: Eliminate a conditionally optimal linear head to isolate feature-learning geometry, but quantify the residual head-suboptimality throughout training.
Treat an empirically observed slow manifold and an exact constrained dynamical system as different claims.
Whiten nuisance covariance before comparing class-mean geometry, while tracking conditioning and rank.
Singular-value equalization is a compact route from class separation to simplex geometry.
Evaluate representation-collapse statistics separately on train and test data and across class imbalance.
A causal neural-collapse study should ablate weight decay, normalization, optimizer, and terminal-training duration.
open_questions: Can closeness to the central path be bounded dynamically for finite-width deep networks?
Do unrenormalized network features follow a conjugate or approximate version of the derived SNR dynamics?
Which parts of MSE neural collapse survive class imbalance, label noise, or more than ten classes?
Is test-set collapse predictive of generalization after controlling for margin and training time?
What roles do batch normalization, weight decay, and SGD noise play in entering and remaining near the central path?
Can the theory handle singular within-class covariance as NC1 progresses?
Does the initial SNR orientation genuinely determine limiting ETF orientation in practical networks?

competitive_landscape.title: Prevalence of Neural Collapse during the terminal phase of deep learning training
competitive_landscape.relationship: foundational empirical neural-collapse study and source of NC1--NC4
competitive_landscape.difference: Papyan et al. document collapse primarily under cross-entropy across seven datasets; this paper establishes analogous MSE measurements, an MSE-specific loss decomposition, and exact dynamics on a renormalized central path.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural collapse with unconstrained features
competitive_landscape.difference: Mixon et al. study empirical-risk geometry and a linearized unconstrained-feature model; this paper adds the least-squares central path, continual covariance renormalization, and explicit closed-form singular-value dynamics.

competitive_landscape.title: A Geometric Analysis of Neural Collapse with Unconstrained Features
competitive_landscape.relationship: direct competing landscape analysis of neural collapse
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhu et al. characterize global minima and strict saddles for a weight-decayed cross-entropy unconstrained-feature model and demonstrate fixed ETF heads; this paper instead follows MSE-specific projected dynamics near a least-squares central path.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Collapse with Cross-Entropy Loss
competitive_landscape.relationship: alternative variational explanation for simplex-ETF geometry
competitive_landscape.difference: Lu and Steinerberger prove the simplex ETF minimizes a constrained cross-entropy feature problem on a hypersphere; this paper derives time dynamics under MSE, least-squares head elimination, and covariance renormalization.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: MSE-trained deep networks exhibit neural collapse, the MSE loss decomposes into collapse-interpretable and least-squares-deviation terms, and exact continually renormalized central-path dynamics predict NC1--NC4.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper presents a 15-combination empirical grid, exact loss identities, measured central-path proximity, a projected SNR flow, and closed-form singular-value asymptotics with full proofs.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The distinctive contribution is the bridge from an exact least-squares decomposition to solvable SNR dynamics. It is a strong mechanistic toy model, but the gap between real deep-network training and the exact unconstrained, zero-decay, continually whitened central path is an assumption gap rather than a proved approximation.

reviewer_notes: Read all 36 cached pages, including empirical appendices, decomposition proofs, the full projected-flow derivation, and the related-work comparison. Four direct competitors were checked against primary arXiv records on 2026-08-23. The reading distinguishes empirical central-path proximity from exact central-path restriction and scopes every theorem to renormalized unconstrained features.
